name: Vorrak
title: The Cinder Maw
summary: A burrowing predator whose grinding jaws can turn a furnace wall into nesting gravel. Its threat comes from mass, heat and territorial certainty.
faction: Unaffiliated fauna; expedition name recorded by the Cinder Mutual.
ecology: Consumes mineral grazers and iron-rich deposits around stable heat. Its six legs distribute weight on fractured crust; the forelimbs excavate while the middle pair brace. It follows sustained ground vibration, not supernatural knowledge of the player.
history: The cooling breach opened a warm nursery basin. Evacuated workers once diverted their hammer shifts away from it; Ithraden has deliberately restarted the loudest presses to drive Vorrak towards intruders.
rivalry: Ithraden steals the heat Vorrak needs and exploits its territorial charges. Open shutters expose the duelist but provoke the animal; rerouting the bypass separates their incentives.
movement: Slow lateral weight transfer precedes a committed forward shove. It can pivot only after lifting a middle brace leg, exposing a narrow safe crossing behind the shoulder.
entrance: A whole slab of the trench floor rises. The grinder jaw emerges first, pushing a dead press aside before the six legs unfold beneath it.

encounter.objective: Transfer the excavation route out of the nursery; drive Vorrak back or kill it, with visibly different ecological consequences.
encounter.arena: An annular trench with four solid basalt islands, weak crust between them and a controllable cooling bypass.

phases.name: Sounding
phases.trigger: First sustained vibration inside its nesting radius.
phases.action: It drums with a front leg; pebbles jump in the lane of an incoming jaw shove.
phases.counterplay: Leave the aligned lane and cross behind the shoulder during the middle-leg reset.

phases.name: Hot ground
phases.trigger: The bypass is opened or two nursery barriers are destroyed.
phases.action: It vents hot breath into a trench, then forces rubble into the resulting steam corridor.
phases.counterplay: Read the jaw’s dull internal heat, climb a solid island and reopen a clear return lane before steam builds.

phases.name: Return path
phases.trigger: A quiet warm route to the nursery is restored.
phases.action: It tests the route with alternating forefeet, then retreats unless attacked or followed.
phases.counterplay: Stop heavy movement, withdraw from the nursery mouth and let its full body clear before restoring the elevator.

encounter.failure: A collapsed crust traps equipment and forces retreat to an upper chain. Destroying the nursery triggers a persistent lethal defence rather than a scripted forgiving reset.
encounter.aftermath: A redirected Vorrak keeps the lower trench inhabited. Killing it opens a faster mining route but removes a major grazer control and changes the later expedition return.

anatomy: Huge six-legged basalt-skinned burrowing predator; broad wedge skull; interlocking mineral grinding lower-jaw plates; load-bearing keratin shoulder ridge; tiny recessed eyes.
materials: Rough living skin, iron-rich keratin, old pale pressure scars, dull heat inside the jaw only.

story.role: The first practical test of Tamsin Reed’s promise that the harbour can be rebuilt without repeating its wartime extraction.

name: Ithraden
title: The Furnace Exile
summary: A furnace tactician who chooses which parts of the arena are survivable. His forged shield arm is a working tool, and he uses it with the intimacy of a veteran operator.
ecology: Needs cooling water, replaceable arm liners and ore shipments. Disabling supply makes him less mobile between heat lanes but never magically deletes his combat skill.
history: Ithraden survived the foundry evacuation and later sold its bypass plans to the occupiers. His exile is a local sentence for that betrayal; no hidden divine pedigree excuses it.
rivalry: He keeps Vorrak agitated as an unwitting perimeter defence, yet fears the animal will break the shutter ring he needs.
movement: Short diagonal steps keep his shield facing heat. His blade controls one narrow lane while the forged forearm braces a shutter; he cannot defend both sides while operating it.
entrance: Behind a furnace wheel, an ordinary human hand wipes soot from a sight slit. The shutter opens, and he advances inside the only band of air cool enough to breathe.

encounter.objective: Stop the siege-alloy shipment and seize or disable the furnace controls.
encounter.arena: Four radial heat lanes separated by masonry wedges; the bypass handwheel sits opposite his initial position.

phases.name: Operating distance
phases.trigger: The challenger enters the control ring.
phases.action: A three-blow blade sequence ends with a shield shove towards a shutter; a visible handwheel movement precedes each heat lane.
phases.counterplay: Dodge across his blade side after the second blow, then punish the planted shield without entering the announced lane.

phases.name: Bleed pressure
phases.trigger: The bypass reduces furnace pressure.
phases.action: He removes an overheated liner and uses it as a short-lived burning barrier, making the shield arm slower until recooled.
phases.counterplay: Let the liner fall, circle through the cooled wedge and interrupt his approach to the water trough.

phases.name: Last shipment
phases.trigger: The lift is seized or the shipment brake is cut.
phases.action: He abandons static control and pursues the lift with direct sword attacks.
phases.counterplay: Use the exposed lift brake to choose the final fighting level; defeat, capture or force him away before the load departs.

encounter.failure: The shipment escapes on a visible lift countdown, supplying Rhaum’s later position. The party can survive and continue with that harder strategic state.
encounter.aftermath: A captured Ithraden is a prisoner with useful knowledge, not automatically redeemed. The furnace can reopen at reduced output under the workers’ own terms.

anatomy: Lean mature male human duelist with close-cropped grey hair, severe visible face, one forged right forearm ending in a broad functional heat shield, long ordinary left-hand blade, soot-worn leather and asymmetric heatproof cloth.
materials: Oxidized iron, heat-bleached leather, thick woven cloth, living human skin.

story.role: A chosen betrayer whose practical competence tempts Garrick Moss to accept an efficient but ruinous bargain.

name: Serath
title: The Reef Ascendant
summary: A thirty-metre hunter whose eight ribbon fins turn a drowned fort into an active feeding current. Beauty and danger are the same physical event.
ecology: Feeds on dense schools concentrated by reef flow. Cartilage and four fin pairs support slow station-keeping and abrupt lateral turns; it cannot follow divers through narrow stone passages.
history: Serath occupied the gulf after the reef matured. The garrison standard now starves the feeding corridor, pushing it into shallower passages where divers work.
rivalry: Morvane’s standard constricts its food supply. Serath attacks the standard’s moving cloth during current reversals and can accidentally break cover the divers depend on.
movement: Broad turns originate in the second fin pair. A folded ventral mouth signals a pass; a widening mouth and inward curl of the rear fins signal a suction strike.
entrance: A school of fish compresses into a silver wall. That wall parts along a curved seam, revealing nacre ribs beneath the passing hunter.

encounter.objective: Reopen the feeding current and survive the hunter’s territorial passes; killing remains possible at major cost to the reef system.
encounter.arena: A central gulf bordered by three air bells and stone channels too narrow for its body, with a sediment-choked living inlet valve.

phases.name: Closed current
phases.trigger: Divers enter the gulf while the inlet is blocked.
phases.action: Serath circles once, then draws loose debris towards its opening mouth.
phases.counterplay: Anchor behind a stone rib when debris starts moving; cross after the mouth closes and the tail clears.

phases.name: Turn of water
phases.trigger: The first sediment obstruction is cleared.
phases.action: The changed current pulls Serath laterally; its inner fins rake the near wall while the opposite flank opens.
phases.counterplay: Read which fin pair flares, use the outer current and work the next obstruction during its wide recovery turn.

phases.name: Feeding passage
phases.trigger: The inlet is fully restored.
phases.action: A shoal enters and Serath commits to a long upstream feeding run.
phases.counterplay: Clear the gulf and remove hanging lines from its route; follow in its wake only after displaced debris settles.

encounter.failure: An unanchored diver is swept to the lower recovery pocket with damaged air gear. Continued obstruction drives the hunter into the shallow route, closing a return path.
encounter.aftermath: A living Serath becomes a known seasonal hazard, not a mount. Successful divers chart its feeding interval for later civilian passage.

anatomy: Thirty-metre pelagic predator with a narrow sculpted head, broad ventral mouth and eight long ribbon fins arranged in four pairs; translucent nacre cartilage visible through thick blue-green skin; no humanoid eyes or dragon horns.
materials: Wet living skin, nacre cartilage, restrained violet sensory pores and clear trailing membrane edges.

story.role: Forces Brigid Vale to distinguish a navigable danger from an enemy that must be eliminated.

name: Morvane
title: The Drowned Standard
summary: A drowned standard-bearer still enforcing the occupation line across a reef that outlived his state.
faction: Voidtouched remnant of a drowned occupying force.
ecology: Bound to the physical standard and the garrison’s surviving command marks. Cannot leave the fortified reef or hear orders from an imagined opened prison.
history: Morvane held the bridge during a refused evacuation. The standard’s residual Shadow corruption preserves a narrow occupation programme, not a faithful personality reconstructed from the dead.
rivalry: Serath’s strikes damage his perimeter; he responds by tightening the standard’s anchoring lines and worsening the reef’s starvation.
movement: Pavise-first lateral shuffles resist current. Every hooked sweep requires the standard to leave its socket, briefly releasing tension in one inlet line.
entrance: A bronze faceplate turns beneath hanging cloth. The submerged bridge is suddenly cleared of drifting silt by a shield planted against the current.

encounter.objective: Remove the occupation standard from the inlet and preserve enough of the bridge for evacuation.
encounter.arena: A submerged bridge with three anchor sockets, a low side channel and two air pockets outside the standard’s sweep.

phases.name: The line holds
phases.trigger: A diver crosses the first command mark.
phases.action: He sweeps the hooked standard at waist height, then thrusts behind the shield; cloth tension indicates the sweep direction.
phases.counterplay: Drop into the side channel during the sweep and strike or release the temporarily slack anchor.

phases.name: Broken socket
phases.trigger: One anchor is released.
phases.action: He drags the pavise to the next socket and pulls a current-driven overhead strike.
phases.counterplay: Watch the standard cloth lift, stay close to the shield’s rear edge and remove the second anchoring pin during the long recovery.

phases.name: No shore to hold
phases.trigger: All anchor sockets are released.
phases.action: The standard loses its fixed sweep and Morvane advances with short heavy thrusts.
phases.counterplay: Lure him clear of the civilians’ bridge, separate him from the fallen standard and disable or contain the residual binding.

encounter.failure: Breaking the bridge isolates an air bell and changes the rescue route. A drowned or exhausted diver is recoverable only while a companion retains an anchored line.
encounter.aftermath: The standard can be secured as dangerous evidence in a sealed transport case. The reef current returns without implying that all Shadow in the world has been cleansed.

anatomy: Tall drowned revenant soldier with an enclosed salt-pitted bronze faceplate, waterlogged dark cloth, a broad cracked stone pavise and a long hooked military standard; no tentacles or coral crown.
materials: Salt deposits, heavy soaked cloth, pitted bronze, chipped basalt; restrained Shadow leakage beneath faceplate.

story.role: A material record of occupation whose defeat gives the divers proof of a suppressed evacuation order.

name: The Marrow Regent
title: Sovereign of the Empty Choir
summary: A resonating burial-ground predator with an ivory bill and six external rib struts. Its call becomes architecture when the bells answer.
faction: Unaffiliated mutated fauna exploited by a Void Ascendant sect.
ecology: Uses low-frequency vibration to disturb burrowing prey, with range amplified by the burial bells. It is not omniscient; textile baffles and disconnected braces limit propagation.
history: The Regent nested in warm ceramic chambers before Vaust arrived. Repeated forced amplification has thickened its resonator tissue and made distant knocks trigger defensive displays.
rivalry: Vaust harvests its tissue and induces calls from the far tuning frame. The animal will pursue him when that stimulus is physically isolated and exposed.
movement: Long deliberate steps keep the torso stable. Before a sonic pulse, the six rib struts spread sequentially and the throat membrane changes from dull plum to stretched pale.
entrance: Dust rises from the floor before any body appears. A smooth bill enters one end of a burial bell and the folding mantle fills its mouth.

encounter.objective: Reach the tuning frame by disabling the forced amplification; redirect or defeat the Regent without destroying the whole burial avenue.
encounter.arena: Three connected bell chambers with movable felt baffles, low side tunnels and visible cedar resonance braces.

phases.name: Listening
phases.trigger: A loud impact travels along a connected brace.
phases.action: The Regent turns its bill towards the source and sends a cone pulse; hanging dust reveals the cone before the main pressure wave.
phases.counterplay: Break line of propagation behind a baffle or move into the next bell through the low side tunnel.

phases.name: Full mantle
phases.trigger: Vaust’s frame forces a second amplification.
phases.action: All six ribs unfold for a broad chamber pulse, followed by a vulnerable closed-mantle recovery.
phases.counterplay: Release a marked brace or brace behind the grounded baffle; cross the chamber while the mantle folds.

phases.name: Uncommanded animal
phases.trigger: The frame’s living resonator is disconnected.
phases.action: It follows the last loud stimulus instead of the artificial signal.
phases.counterplay: Create a deliberate sound route away from custodians, then keep the evacuation corridor quiet.

encounter.failure: Repeated bell destruction erases inscriptions and sends the animal towards the occupied annex. Custodian rescue becomes a separate timed consequence.
encounter.aftermath: A redirected animal retains a nesting chamber beyond a damped barrier. The name Regent remains an expedition epithet; no throne or cosmic station is established.

anatomy: Huge flightless birdlike predator with an elongated smooth ivory bill and a high narrow torso; six curved external rib struts form a folding resonator mantle, muscular dark featherless legs; no humanoid skull, antlers or crown.
materials: Aged ivory keratin, taut charcoal skin, chalk dust, dull plum throat membrane.

story.role: Makes Sabine Rook choose which evidence can be carried and which must be protected in place.

name: Vaust
title: The Bell Surgeon
summary: A calm acoustician who treats the burial avenue as a weapon he can finish while fighting you.
ecology: A mortal operator dependent on intact bells, measured sightlines and a harvested resonator. His advantage is prepared transmission paths rather than unbounded voice magic.
history: Vaust adapted civilian surveying methods for siege range-finding. He chose the burial avenue because its custodians could not move their records quickly enough to resist occupation.
rivalry: He needs the Regent alive but tractable. The animal’s independent movement continually disrupts his calibration, giving an observant challenger opportunities he cannot entirely control.
movement: Economical sideways steps place a bell between him and an attacker. He commits both hands to each long tuning stroke and uses the hammer’s hooked heel for close defence.
entrance: Three gentle hammer taps arrive from different chambers. At the far frame, Vaust adjusts an ear guard and writes down how long your footsteps took to answer.

encounter.objective: Prevent the calibrated pulse from reaching the occupied annex and capture or destroy the firing method.
encounter.arena: A tuning platform overlooking the bell avenue, three transmission braces and a hanging resonator frame.

phases.name: Calibration
phases.trigger: The challenger reaches the final bell.
phases.action: He taps a brace, waits for its return and strikes the hammer where the echo predicts movement.
phases.counterplay: Change elevation after the first tap; the returning dust line marks the attack path.

phases.name: Live measurement
phases.trigger: Two braces are damped or severed.
phases.action: He moves the resonator to a surviving line and sweeps a wire frame at close range to force distance.
phases.counterplay: Close during the transfer, attack the support hand or pin the frame without standing in its line.

phases.name: Premature discharge
phases.trigger: The annex firing path is interrupted.
phases.action: He attempts a direct overload that will shatter the nearest bell and cover his retreat.
phases.counterplay: Read the rapid, irregular tapping; release the frame counterweight or force him off the grounded firing plate before the final strike.

encounter.failure: An undamped path carries a destructive pulse into the annex, injuring custodians and destroying specific records. This loss persists even if Vaust is killed afterwards.
encounter.aftermath: Surviving plans can establish how the acoustic cell supports the exterior siege. A living Vaust remains an accountable enemy with his own strategy.

anatomy: Compact older male human with bald scarred head and measured expression; fitted dark work coat and ceramic ear guards; holds a long tuning hammer and a wire-framed cracked resonator; no medical gore.
materials: Chipped ceramic, worn steel, waxed linen, ordinary mature skin.

story.role: An antagonist who destroys evidence for military advantage, establishing the trilogy’s conflict over what can be proved.

name: Orryx
title: The Briar Cataphract
summary: An armoured canopy hunter that can climb the structures its opponents mistake for safety.
ecology: Territorial near its molting shelf and clutch. Four locomotor legs carry the thorax; two raised blade forelimbs hook prey and terrain. It senses transmitted vibration better than motion through open air.
history: The old aqueduct offers reliable drumming surfaces above a flooded ravine. Survey traffic has concentrated during its breeding season, creating a conflict that did not exist at lower footfall.
rivalry: Serevra uses its territorial boundaries to protect her platform, but refuses to destroy its clutch because doing so would drive it through both expeditions’ camps.
movement: Stops completely before a two-stage hook and pull. After climbing, its rear legs must find purchase before the blade limbs can strike again.
entrance: A blade limb hooks over an aqueduct edge. Roots snap one at a time as the narrow thorax rises into the morning light.

encounter.objective: Open a supply crossing by rerouting vibration or defeating the animal; keep the nesting shelf separate from the crossing objective.
encounter.arena: Two aqueduct spans, a hanging root bridge and a white watch pier, with water sluices that can mask or redirect sound.

phases.name: Claimed span
phases.trigger: A heavy footstep reaches its nearest pier.
phases.action: It hooks the span, then pulls its head into a forward snapping strike; the hook remains visible before the pull.
phases.counterplay: Leave the hooked edge, cross behind its raised limb and attack only during the rear-leg purchase pause.

phases.name: High approach
phases.trigger: The direct span is flooded or its first perch fails.
phases.action: It climbs through roots and drops a blade across the next landing.
phases.counterplay: Watch root tension and falling moss; stay on an unconnected rope line or move to a pier outside that root network.

phases.name: Crossing window
phases.trigger: The old water channel is reopened.
phases.action: Water masks the supply party while Orryx turns towards a prepared drumming lure.
phases.counterplay: Stop using the resonant stone route and escort the convoy across the quieter root bridge before the lure breaks.

encounter.failure: A severed root bridge isolates supplies. Killing the clutch makes Orryx abandon predictable defence for a pursuit through the camps.
encounter.aftermath: The reopened channel supports future seasonal crossings; the field guide records a closure during the next molt instead of declaring the forest conquered.

anatomy: Massive six-legged forest arthropod with a low forward-armoured head, tall segmented thorax and two long folded blade forelimbs held above four locomotor legs; thornlike growth only along chitin joints, no mammal eyes.
materials: Matte dark olive chitin, reddish joint membranes, wet moss caught in grooves.

story.role: Introduces Corvin Holt’s conflict between a survey deadline and the living conditions a map must describe.

name: Serevra
title: The Pale Huntress
summary: A formidable ranger whose claim is practical and limited: she built a rescue route, and she will not let a better-funded expedition take it by force.
faction: Independent Pale Line expedition; proposed Gate-Touched mortal.
ecology: Needs dry bowstrings, recovered arrows and concealed rope exits. Wind and water affect her range; neither pale camouflage nor Gate training makes her invisible.
history: Serevra lost her original route to a ravine collapse, rebuilt the aqueduct approach and rescued two stranded surveyors. Her contract now gives her crew a legitimate access claim contested by the Meridian Survey.
rivalry: She understands Orryx’s nesting radius but cannot command it. Using the animal as a weapon risks the rescue route that gives her claim its moral and contractual weight.
movement: A single planted draw alternates with rapid lateral relocation along prepared ropes. Her release shoulder and bow cant disclose whether the next shot pins cover or targets movement.
entrance: An arrow cuts the loose end of a rope beside your hand. She stands on the distant white pier, gives her name and states the boundary once.

encounter.objective: Win passage through a declared contest, negotiate shared access or survive a hostile crossing; surrender remains a valid outcome.
encounter.arena: Three sighted piers and two rope exits with a clearly marked noncombat shelter for both crews.

phases.name: Declared measure
phases.trigger: A challenger accepts the crossing contest or breaches the boundary.
phases.action: She fires a visible ranging arrow, then attempts a pinning shot at the route it marks.
phases.counterplay: Change routes after the ranging shot, use stone cover and close only when her bow arm is extended.

phases.name: Broken sightline
phases.trigger: The challenger reaches the second pier.
phases.action: She releases a prepared rope and descends to a lower firing shelf.
phases.counterplay: Watch the escape knot move; secure the upper rope or use water spray to reveal the new angle.

phases.name: Within reach
phases.trigger: The challenger reaches her platform or meets the agreed score.
phases.action: She transitions to short bow strikes and a draw held at close range, then acknowledges a clean disarm or boundary loss.
phases.counterplay: Do not attack the noncombat shelter; use a controlled disarm, accept mutual withdrawal or state the negotiated claim.

encounter.failure: Harming the shelter ends the legitimate contest and turns both crews against the challenger. Losing the contest costs access time rather than a mandatory death.
encounter.aftermath: A fair resolution makes Serevra a recurring competitor who can cooperate without becoming subordinate. A violent seizure creates a durable human rivalry.

anatomy: Adult human woman ranger with weathered brown skin, tightly bound black braids, pale ash camouflage cloak cut short at bow arm, long asymmetric recurved bow and simple bone range markers; believable athletic proportions.
materials: Tough barkcloth, hide, dark wood, worn steel, rain on skin.

story.role: A rival with reasons to win, forcing Corvin to earn a professional relationship rather than collect a follower.

name: The Sundered Engine
title: A Sun Without a Master
summary: A solar artillery construct whose obsolete map turns a functioning road into an enemy approach.
faction: Abandoned Forged military apparatus; no active allegiance.
ecology: Depends on direct sunlight, intact mirror facets and functional leg joints. Clouds reduce beam output but do not stop its physical bracing and shutter attacks.
history: The Engine survived the fortress’s last storm with one map plate and a damaged targeting linkage. It cannot distinguish the relocated civilian road from the former assault ramp.
rivalry: Rhaum wants its map plate replaced with his own firing plan. The Engine currently treats his ammunition lift as an unauthorised approach and destroys the supplies he needs.
movement: Two arms brace before the chest mirror rotates; the other pair move shutter plates. Its mass prevents an immediate reversal after it commits to a ramp.
entrance: A mirror shadow passes over the evacuation cistern. Above it, the construct plants all four arms and raises its chest towards the sun.

encounter.objective: Defocus the array or replace the obsolete road-denial instruction without letting Rhaum capture the targeting assembly.
encounter.arena: A stepped firing ring with three shadow pockets, two manual observation shutters and a reachable rear maintenance platform.

phases.name: Find the sun
phases.trigger: Direct sunlight reaches the chest mirror.
phases.action: A broad pale reflection narrows into a beam that sweeps one ramp.
phases.counterplay: Move during the broad reflection and stay inside a hard shadow; attack a brace joint after the sweep stops.

phases.name: Manual defence
phases.trigger: Two targeting shutters are jammed.
phases.action: It advances with heavy shutter-plate strikes and repositions to a new solar angle.
phases.counterplay: Read which brace arm lifts, cross beneath the opposite shutter and ride the maintenance lift while the legs reset.

phases.name: Defocus window
phases.trigger: The rear maintenance platform is reached.
phases.action: The chest mirror locks for recalibration, exposing the defocus linkage while a timed mechanical sweep clears the platform.
phases.counterplay: Anchor before the sweep, operate the linkage between passes and choose permanent defocus or a restricted civilian-safe map.

encounter.failure: A destroyed cistern exit forces the evacuation column onto the exposed road. Leaving the map plate intact for Rhaum strengthens his later artillery position.
encounter.aftermath: Permanent defocus leaves a heavy but non-artillery salvage machine. A revised map creates a limited guardian of the passage with explicit maintenance obligations.

anatomy: Twenty-metre four-armed military construct with a short broad torso, two massive load-bearing legs and a broken concave mirror embedded in its chest; one pair of arms braces, the other aims heavy shutter plates; no humanoid glowing face.
materials: Tarnished bronze, cut dark stone, real mirror facets, heavy joints and pale ceramic heat liners.

story.role: An encounter about operational responsibility whose consequences determine whether Tamsin’s supply route stays open.

name: Rhaum
title: The Last Artillerist
summary: A siege captain who can make one narrow ramp impossible to cross, until the logistics supporting him are broken.
faction: Void Ascendants, high citadel artillery detachment.
ecology: Carries limited charged ammunition and needs prepared recoil notches. His harness distributes load but cannot let him fire the heavy cannon accurately while running.
history: Rhaum commanded a failed valley siege and now seeks a weapon that will remove his dependence on ordinary crews. His fear of another defeat drives calculated expendability, not a secret wish to be saved.
rivalry: The Sundered Engine denies his supply lift. He alternates attempts to capture it with volleys that further damage the mirror he hopes to command.
movement: Moves slowly between pre-sighted buttresses, then locks the harness into a notch. A kneeling recoil stance and visible breech vent distinguish a full shot from a short suppressing discharge.
entrance: A cannon report arrives before the captain is visible. Stone chips fall from the only ramp wide enough for the waiting evacuation wagons.

encounter.objective: Break the artillery position and keep the civilian supply lift operational.
encounter.arena: A zigzag ramp with four firing notches, destructible upper parapets and an ammunition lift on a visible cycle.

phases.name: Range held
phases.trigger: The challenger leaves the cistern cover.
phases.action: He vents the breech, locks into a notch and fires a straight penetrating shot; the vent precedes the muzzle charge.
phases.counterplay: Move across the lane during venting and close under the notch’s minimum depression angle.

phases.name: Ammunition denied
phases.trigger: The supply lift is stopped or two ammunition crates are seized.
phases.action: He uses short suppressing blasts and shoves with the barrel while moving towards his reserve.
phases.counterplay: Force movement between notches, attack the exposed harness buckle and keep the reserve physically separated.

phases.name: Last charged round
phases.trigger: Only his visibly marked reserve round remains.
phases.action: He commits to a long charge aimed at the civilian lift brake.
phases.counterplay: Interrupt the planted stance, pull the lift behind the stone sill or redirect the shot by rotating the damaged recoil notch.

encounter.failure: The civilian lift brake breaks and the evacuation must use a slower route; surviving supplies determine how many loads can be recovered before night.
encounter.aftermath: Seized artillery records expose the timing of Draeven’s blockade. Rhaum’s capture or death changes military intelligence, not the world’s metaphysical order.

anatomy: Broad older human siege captain in a practical dark military coat, weathered metal shoulder brace, bare stern face, carrying a massive shoulder-mounted recoil-balanced arcane cannon supported by a belt harness; no full-body ornamental armour.
materials: Worn steel, soot, stiff wool, leather harness, faint energy deep inside breech.

story.role: Connects the furnace shipment to the harbour campaign and makes earlier resource choices alter a later encounter.

name: The Unfaced Pilgrim
title: Bearer of the Missing Step
summary: A traveller-shaped phenomenon that repeats a route one step out of agreement with its own shadow.
faction: Unaffiliated bounded spatial manifestation; ontology unresolved.
ecology: Exists only inside the Lacuna chamber and responds to occupied stair positions. It does not hunt beyond the doorway or turn ordinary darkness into evil.
history: Three survey parties recorded the figure with different clothing details but the same displaced step. The collection preserves those reports as disputed observations rather than an omniscient origin story.
rivalry: Ultharen closes routes the Pilgrim has just crossed. Whether this is cooperation, maintenance or coincidental rule interaction remains unresolved; the observable timing is consistent.
movement: Moves at walking speed on marked steps. Its ceiling shadow commits one step ahead; it cannot change that announced destination during the same footfall.
entrance: A wet footprint appears on a dry ceiling stair. Below it, a tall cloth-folded figure descends into the place your next step would occupy.

encounter.objective: Recover the missing surveyor’s tether and establish a traversable return without assuming the manifestation must die.
encounter.arena: Five marked landings in one chamber, an ordinary doorway and a ceiling return visible from the central landing.

phases.name: One step early
phases.trigger: The entrant occupies the second marked landing.
phases.action: The ceiling shadow selects a destination; the figure then reaches across the corresponding real step.
phases.counterplay: Read the shadow’s foot before moving and choose the unoccupied adjacent landing.

phases.name: Crossed route
phases.trigger: A tether is attached to the blocked junction.
phases.action: The figure follows the tether’s sequence in reverse, closing distance on anyone who repeats their own path.
phases.counterplay: Use an unused side step, maintain the external anchor and let the announced route complete before doubling back.

phases.name: Ordinary rain
phases.trigger: The blocked tether is returned to the entrance line.
phases.action: It walks to the threshold and stops with one foot inside the chamber.
phases.counterplay: Carry the recovered surveyor out while preserving the external anchor; attacking at the threshold restarts its local sequence.

encounter.failure: A misread step returns the entrant to the previous landing and abrades the tether. Exhausting the tether leaves a harder recovery route, not an arbitrary cosmological punishment.
encounter.aftermath: The Pilgrim remains an observable unresolved presence. A successful chart records reliable behaviours and explicitly omits a claimed true origin.

anatomy: Very tall lean figure whose head is a folded hollow of matte ivory cloth rather than a face; long jointed hands visible, feet ordinary and grounded, severe charcoal travel layers, one plain stone staff.
materials: Matte cloth, dry stone, weathered bare hands; no black smoke cloud.

story.role: Tests Jolant Grey’s willingness to publish an incomplete but useful account.

name: Ultharen
title: The Folded Colossus
summary: A moving arrangement of immense arches that changes which parts of a stair are neighbours.
ecology: Its hinges and stone supports require physical contact with the chamber. It cannot fold external mountains, create worlds or rewrite history.
history: Old abrasion marks imply configurations predating the road crews. Those marks support a history of movement, not a verified account of construction or intelligence.
rivalry: Its rotation follows the Pilgrim’s completed crossings by one interval. Stopping an arch interrupts that pattern but makes no claim about which entity has authority.
movement: Four blunt supports reposition before an arch turns. Dust sheds from the next active hinge, and the empty central volume remains a stable landmark during rotation.
entrance: The landing in front of you rises slowly. What seemed to be a doorway lifts on four supports, revealing another stair behind its empty centre.

encounter.objective: Lock a safe route long enough to extract trapped surveyors and their evidence.
encounter.arena: The same bounded Lacuna chamber, with three rotating arches, five marked landings and two accessible friction locks.

phases.name: New neighbours
phases.trigger: The first surveyor tether crosses its central arch.
phases.action: An arch turns ninety degrees, exchanging two connected landings; hinge dust announces the turning side.
phases.counterplay: Stand on a marked landing outside the hinge sweep and cross only after the stone contacts settle.

phases.name: Load rejection
phases.trigger: A friction lock is inserted.
phases.action: The construct raises one support and drops a short crushing load onto the blocked joint.
phases.counterplay: Leave the support’s shadow, brace the lock from the remote socket and use the unloaded arch to reach the second mechanism.

phases.name: Held configuration
phases.trigger: Both friction locks engage.
phases.action: The remaining free arch cycles slowly to shed excess load.
phases.counterplay: Time the extraction through its empty centre, remove nonessential weight and leave the locks engaged until the last tether clears.

encounter.failure: An overloaded lock breaks and rearranges the route while the people remain on marked landings. Recovery requires a longer physical circuit; no character vanishes by unexplained fiat.
encounter.aftermath: The chamber can be mapped in a documented held state. Long-term stability remains unproven and must not be advertised as a permanent portal network.

anatomy: Nonhumanoid walking architectural creature composed of three immense interlocking pale stone arches on four blunt jointed supports; an empty central volume, no face, no runes or orb core.
materials: Ancient limestone, black friction marks, dust shed from articulated contacts.

story.role: Turns a mystery into an engineering extraction without resolving its metaphysical origin.
